slides.heading: Logical AND
slides.body: Logical AND is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Logical AND
slides.body: The and operator is True only when both conditions are True. It is useful when all requirements must be satisfied.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: and is like entering a library that requires both an ID and a library card. Missing one means you cannot enter.

slides.heading: Example: Logical AND
slides.code:
age = 20
has_id = True
print(age >= 18 and has_id)

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Check if a student passed and submitted a project.

quiz.prompt_text: When does the and operator return True?

options: When at least one condition is True
When the first condition is False

quiz.explanation: Exactly right! The and operator requires both conditions to be True. If even one is False, the entire expression evaluates to False.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to check if a person is at least 18 and has a valid ID.
quiz.explanation: Both variables are assigned first, and only then can the and expression check both conditions together in print().

quiz.prompt_text: Check if a student passed their exam and submitted their project, then print the result.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(passed and submitted) outputs True only when both are True. The and operator is perfect for enforcing that all requirements are met.
